newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge up, Ireland's EBR data awaited.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge up, Ireland's EBR data awaited.

text.p: Irish government bonds edged upwards in thin late trade on Friday in line with Europe as the market awaited the release of Ireland's 1996 Exchequer Borrowing Requirement data, dealers said.
The data, due out at 1630 GMT, is expected to be well below target at 250 to 400 million punts, helped by strong growth in tax revenues, economists said.
Dealers said they did not expect any surprises in the data which they said should confirm a very positive borrowing situation in Ireland.

"The market has held up quite well. It is up marginally in line with Europe. One might have expected Thursday's strong domestic credit numbers to keep Irish bonds down but that has not happened," one dealer said.
"International players still see Ireland as value and that has supported the market here," the dealer added.

By 1550 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained 12 pence from Thursday's close at 101.12 to yield 6.12 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had gained 20 pence from the close at 108.15 to yield 6.81 percent.
